title: Minimax Causal-Slope Risk with Latent Environments under Dual Weak Identification Strength
banked_reason: Sound partial results remain below the field floor: unequal exponential coefficients permit polynomially different risk envelopes, leaving the minimax crossover unresolved.

proof_attempt_summary: Three discovery solve rounds produced sound benchmark results and one substantial full-law salvage attempt added exact-twin and tangent lemmas. The original matched minimax frontier remains open because legal approximate-pair localization, the composite relative-tail prefactor, and a uniformly attaining fitted branch test were not established. Math review passed, but the achieved incremental package was below the field floor; no Lean formalization was launched.
tldr:
The finite estimator theorem proves the original-data causal-slope risk bracket
\[
 c\min\{1,(n\delta^2)^{-1}+e^{-C n\eta^2}\}
 \le R_n(\delta,\eta)
 \le C\min\{1,(n\delta^2)^{-1}+e^{-c n\eta^2}\}.
\]
One total finite covariance-and-robust-cumulant estimator attains its upper side with all nuisance coordinates unknown. The model is a strict compact Gaussian--Hermite subclass of Kivva et al.'s equation-(6) alpha-shift class. Minimax risk tends to zero along public-strength sequences exactly when \(n\delta^2\to\infty\) and \(n\eta^2\to\infty\). The continuous rate is matched above the theorem's sufficient logarithmic threshold, and fixed positive strengths give order \(n^{-1}\). This round adds a certified three-variable evaluation of the global exact-twin coefficient, the curve-wise Gaussian covariance tangent profile, and uniform exact-twin Chernoff exponent transfer in the logarithmic crossover. It does not establish the composite testing prefactor or a matched crossover frontier. Lower bounds transfer to compatibly bounded superclasses by inclusion; the estimator and upper bound do not.
gap: Population environmental identification and local weak-identification inference do not evaluate \(R_n(\delta,\eta)\) with both strengths varying independently and all benchmark nuisance coordinates unknown.
fill: An evaluated matched frontier combines legal density comparisons, nuisance profiling, and finite observed-density tests. Identification and covariance algebra support the kernel; they do not replace it.
